item.title: Betti Sequences of Four-Generated Non-Almost-Symmetric Nearly Gorenstein Numerical Semigroup Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.05788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a minimally four-generated numerical semigroup that is nearly Gorenstein but not almost symmetric, and let $R=k[S]$ over an arbitrary field $k$. We prove that the defining ideal of $R$ has four or five minimal generators when $R$ has Cohen--Macaulay type two, and exactly six when it has type three. Thus the total Betti sequence over the four-variable polynomial presentation ring is one of $$(1,4,5,2),\quad (1,5,6,2),\quad (1,6,8,3),$$ and all three possibilities occur. The type-three argument uses a canonical-ideal exact sequence, a chain-level comparison on $\operatorname{Tor}$, and a codimension-three Gorenstein reduction. The resulting classification gives an affirmative answer, over every field, to Moscariello and Strazzanti's Question 4.3 on four-generated nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups that are not almost symmetric.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Lin Zhang

item.title: Uniform comparison of multiplier and test ideals for polynomials with affinely independent support
item.description: arXiv:2611.05914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f\in\Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ have affinely independent exponent vectors. We prove that its test ideals agree with the reductions of its multiplier ideals at all nonnegative real exponents for every sufficiently large prime in one arithmetic progression. The progression depends only on the support of $f$.
item.dc:creator: Takafumi Shibuta

item.title: Intersection Product Formulas and Integral Dependence
item.description: arXiv:2611.06370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the intersection product formulas of Gaffney and Gassler for polar multiplicities and Segre numbers over arbitrary Noetherian local rings. For equidimensional and universally catenary rings, we give a geometric refinement of the Principle of Specialization of Integral Dependence, in which the maximal dimension of the images of exceptional components mapping into the hypersurface determines a precise Segre number that strictly increases.
item.dc:creator: Yairon Cid-Ruiz, Steven Dale Cutkosky

item.title: Ideals of 2-minors of nearly determinantal matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.06571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce nearly determinantal matrices and study their ideals of $2$-minors. We classify nearly determinantal matrices whose ideals of $2$-minors are prime. Furthermore, we characterize those nearly determinantal matrices whose ideals of $2$-minors are prime and Cohen--Macaulay with linear resolutions.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

item.title: Capelli Operators and the Bernstein-Sato polynomials of Minors
item.description: arXiv:2611.06030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every ideal of minors of a generic complex matrix, we determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein-Sato polynomial. These roots lie in explicit rational intervals indexed by the rank strata. Every nonintegral root is simple, whereas the multiplicity of each integral root equals the number of labels producing that root. We deduce the strong motivic monodromy conjecture, including the inequality relating pole orders to root multiplicities; for minors of size $r$, the largest possible root multiplicity over all matrix dimensions is $\lfloor\sqrt{4r-1}\rfloor$. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal ideal, root multiplicities, strong monodromy conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Chen, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: Homology and Topology of Partially Ordered Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.06261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a unified homology theory for directed partial orders (DPOs) and lattice-ordered positive cones on fields of characteristic zero. With the underlying field and its operations fixed, we define order?carrying spaces independently by topological conditions, establish a bijection with DPO positive cones, and characterize lattice orders by intersections of minimal open neighborhoods. A unified comparison theorem identifies graded Ext for region ideals with sheaf cohomology and multiplicative Tor with the reduced singular homology of truncated regions, giving a topological interpretation of the existence and preservation of reduced decompositions. We obtain canonical cohomological obstructions to lattice ordering, prove that a coefficient module for positive multiplication is flat if and only if the multiplier has a positive inverse, and show that every strict extension of positive cones on the same field produces a nonzero first Tor obstruction. Finally, we place the concrete lattice recently constructed by Bao-Zhang within this framework.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhen Bao

item.title: Mixed linkage of numerical semigroup ideals
item.description: arXiv:2604.14478v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce principal and canonical linkage for relative ideals of a numerical semigroup $S$ and study their interaction modulo translation. On normalized $S$-reflexive ideals, a principal link followed by a canonical link acts by addition of the canonical ideal $K$. The resulting mixed components have paths as their underlying simple graphs, and their even liaison classes are chains under inclusion. If $r(K)$ is the positive reduction number of $K$, every even class has at most $r(K)$ elements and every mixed component has at most $2r(K)$ vertices. For components with a loop, the bound improves to $r(K)$. For semigroups of type two, we compute the even class of a given ideal from its occupied and gap blocks along arithmetic progressions and prove that the largest even class has exactly $r(K)$ elements. This equality can fail in type three. Both component bounds are sharp, and explicit families of embedding dimension three give components of unbounded size with and without loops.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Ojeda

item.title: Hilbert Series in Four Variables and Linear Factors of High Multiplicity
item.description: arXiv:2608.24797v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Explicit sequences of forms with the Hilbert series predicted by Fr\"oberg's conjecture are difficult to construct beyond the almost complete intersection case. Over a field of characteristic zero, we prove that six forms of degree $d\ge4$ in four variables cannot have the predicted series if each is divisible by a power of a linear form with exponent at least $(15d+91)/16$. A power of the product of six quadric cones gives a nonzero element of the inverse system in a degree where the predicted series vanishes. This obstruction implies that every fixed-order Taylor truncation of the homogeneous Rogers--Szeg\H{o} polynomial at $q=1$ fails to complete five powers of linear forms to the predicted series in all sufficiently large degrees. As a fixed-degree counterpart, we use exact certificates to prove the conjecture for any number of general quintics or septics; together with known results, this establishes the equal-degree conjecture in four variables for $1\le d\le9$.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang

item.title: $\mathrm{v}$-numbers of powers of edge ideals of cubic circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27545v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide the exact formula for the $\mathrm{v}$-number of powers of the edge ideal of a cubic circulant graph $C_{2n}(a,n)$ with $1\le a<n$.
item.dc:creator: Guangjun Zhu, Jiaxin Li, Yulin Hu

item.title: Coherence and the Hilbert-syzygy identity for power series over valuation domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.05246v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $V$ be a complete valuation domain of rank 1, and let $\Gamma$ be its value group. We investigate the power series ring $V[[t]]$, and finally answer the long standing question of when this ring is coherent. Specifically, we prove that it is coherent if and only if $V$ is almost maximal, and either $\Gamma = \mathbb{R}$ or $\Gamma$ is discrete. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the weak Hilbert-syzygy identity $w. dim V [[X]] = w. dim V + 1$ holds if and only if $V[[X]]$ is a coherent ring.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui, Adam Jones, Yiding Wang
